name: Asterix DN404 NFT transfer resolves ownership from a truncated id but clears the approval of the full id
summary: Asterix (ASTX) embeds an early DN404 whose _transferFromNFT resolves the owner and rewrites ownership through _ownershipIndex(id) = id << 1, which drops the top bit, but checks and deletes tokenApprovals[id] under the full id. The attacker approved a helper for its NFT 4598, then in a Uniswap v4 unlock sold one ASTX into the ETH/ASTX pool by calling the mirror's transferFrom(attacker, PoolManager, 2^255 + 4598), took about 0.013 ETH, and had the helper pull NFT 4598 and its ASTX back from the PoolManager with the surviving approval; 100 such sales per transaction over 242 transactions took 26.75 ETH from the pool.

campaign.selection: transactions from attacker EOA 0x7a9514e73554d9bea1d69335dd2ba7798cc82328 calling atInversebrah (contract creation) after the anchor; each repeats the sale-and-pullback loop against the ASTX mirror 0x0000000000c26fabfe894d13233d5ec73f61cc72 and takes ETH from the Uniswap v4 PoolManager

notes: Reset: initialize(mirror) by the owner 71 blocks after the token's deployment (0x15d380d0, block 19214012), which linked the DN404 mirror 0x0000000000c26fabfe894d13233d5ec73f61cc72 (slot 0xa20d6e21d0e5255309) and minted the supply; the exploit's NFT transfers only reach _transferFromNFT through that mirror. The token is not a proxy; the only later owner write (0x23b848ff, block 19364466) set maxBalanceLimitLocked. The Uniswap v4 ETH/ASTX pool is where the value sat, not part of the defective code.

Earliest exploit: the mirror's ERC721 Transfer log carries the id as passed. Of 57,075 non-mint, non-burn mirror transfers from deployment to the block before the anchor none has an id above 10,000; from the anchor to block 26,000,000 the only ones with ids of 2^32 or more are the 242 transactions of EOA 0x7a9514e7 (blocks 25267746-25269320), funded on 2026-06-06 and otherwise idle. campaign.mjs on selector 0xe5eb36c8 capped at 3,000 candidates and found only ordinary NFT transfers.

Loss: loss.mjs over the anchor and the 241 campaign transactions with the PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90 as victim; its ASTX nets to zero in each transaction (sold in, pulled back), so the depletion is the pool's ETH. Asterix reported about 30 ETH over 242 transactions; SlowMist about $40k.

The same early-DN404 id-truncation flaw was exploited at Flooring Protocol V2 and BitmapPunks (BT404) around the same day. Those are other projects' contracts, and the Asterix attacker EOA 0x7a9514e7 sent transactions only to ASTX, its mirror and the Universal Router, so they are separate incidents, not this campaign.
